title: Civil first appeal where the previous advocate filed nothing for eleven months

input.text: Decree against our client in a partition suit, preliminary decree, eleven months ago. Previous advocate told the client an appeal was 'being prepared'. Nothing was filed. Client now wants us to file the first appeal with a delay condonation. We have the decree, the judgment, and a set of the trial pleadings from the client's own file. Certified copies not obtained. Previous advocate is not responding to calls. Grounds: the trial court excluded the 1987 family settlement and treated a post-1994 revenue entry as conclusive. Two questions — is the delay condonable at all, and how do we handle the previous advocate's non-cooperation without making him a party?

triage.oneLineRead: Eleven-month delay with no filing, no certified copies, an unresponsive previous advocate, and a limitation question that turns on whether the delay is explained day by day.

issueMap.issue: Whether an eleven-month delay is condonable
issueMap.note: Condonation is discretionary and fact-dependent. Eleven months is long but not fatal; the explanation must be specific and supported, not 'counsel did not file'.

issueMap.issue: Whether the previous advocate's inaction is a sufficient cause
issueMap.note: Client inaction is usually fatal; counsel inaction is more forgivable but needs a factual record. The two are often mixed and that is where applications fail.

issueMap.issue: Whether the client did anything in the eleven months
issueMap.note: Any letter, visit or call to the previous advocate becomes the spine of the application.

issueMap.issue: Whether the 1987 family settlement was proved or merely marked
issueMap.note: Exclusion on a legal ground is a far better ground than exclusion on weight.

issueMap.issue: Whether the decree is preliminary and therefore appealable
issueMap.note: Appealability of a preliminary decree is settled, but the framing must be exact or the appeal will be met with a maintainability objection.

Memo of Appeal — Substantial Questions and Grounds
drafts.body:
SYNTHETIC / DEMO — gate-shaped worked example; NOT filing-ready. [PENDING] holes are deliberate.

MEMO OF APPEAL — SUBSTANTIAL QUESTIONS AND GROUNDS
In the High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan at Jodhpur (first appeal from a Jodhpur district decree).

Cause title (complete from the decree): Appellant [client]; Respondent [ ]; in the partition suit in which the preliminary decree was passed.

Statutory frame:
  - First appeal from an original decree — CPC 1908, s. 96 r/w O. 41 r. 1 (VERIFIED).
  - Limitation — Limitation Act 1963, Art. 116, 90 days (SECONDARY; article reference to be confirmed).
  - Condonation, if needed, is a separate application — Limitation Act 1963, s. 5 (VERIFIED).
Gate from the file: citationGate BLOCKED; limitationGate EXPIRED-RISK.

Facts relied on (from the file): partition suit; preliminary decree passed 11 months ago; the trial court excluded the 1987 family settlement and relied on a post-1994 revenue entry as conclusive. The 1987 settlement is a photocopy; whether it was proved or only marked is UNCONFIRMED.

SUBSTANTIAL QUESTIONS / GROUNDS (fact plus law — first appeal):
  1. That the exclusion of the 1987 family settlement is a legal error going to admissibility, not a weighing error. [PENDING — it is a photocopy; if it required registration or was never proved, the exclusion may be correct.]
  2. That treating the post-1994 revenue entry as conclusive is an error of law. [PENDING — no named authority on the evidentiary value of a revenue entry in the file.]
  3. Maintainability — the decree is preliminary and therefore appealable; the framing must be kept exact to meet any maintainability objection. (Core: CPC 1908, s. 96 r/w O. 41 r. 1, VERIFIED.)

Caveat: this memo must be filed WITH the certified judgment and decree (CPC O. 41 r. 1). Certified copies not yet obtained. File the memo and any s. 5 application together only once the client's delay affidavit can be sworn truthfully.

drafts.title: Letter to Previous Advocate — Record and No-Objection
drafts.body:
SYNTHETIC / DEMO — gate-shaped worked example; NOT filing-ready. [PENDING] holes are deliberate.

[On the letterhead of the advocate]
Date: [date of dispatch to be inserted]
To: [previous advocate's name and address, from the client's file]
Subject: Partition suit — [cause title] — preliminary decree — request for the trial record and a no-objection.

Respected Sir,
  1. We have been approached by [client], who was your client in the above partition suit in which a preliminary decree was passed 11 months ago.
  2. We are instructed to file a first appeal before the Rajasthan High Court, Jodhpur (CPC 1908, s. 96 r/w O. 41 r. 1, VERIFIED).
  3. We are told nothing was filed after the decree. We make no allegation; we only record that we are instructed to carry the matter forward.
  4. We request you to hand over, or permit us to inspect and copy: (a) the complete trial record — pleadings, issues and order sheets; (b) the certified copy of the judgment and the preliminary decree, if you hold one; (c) the exhibit number and status of the 1987 family settlement and the 1994 revenue entry.
  5. We also request your no-objection to our appearance. This is a courtesy and a record-protection measure; it is not a legal precondition, and we shall file on our client's fresh vakalatnama regardless. (Practice, Rajasthan — SECONDARY.)
  6. We are separately applying for certified copies, so this request is not load-bearing.

Kindly treat this as urgent and favour us with an early reply. [PENDING — dispatch proof to be preserved on file.]
Yours faithfully,
[advocate]

checklist: Certified copies of judgment and decree — apply today
Client's own record of every follow-up: dates, mode, who spoke to whom
Any WhatsApp or call log with the previous advocate
Certified copy of the 1987 settlement or its exhibit number
Trial court's exact reason for excluding the settlement
Whether the client paid the previous advocate and any receipt
Whether the decree has been executed in the meantime
Substantial question of law formulation — this is a first appeal, so frame it as fact plus law

terminalOutcome.label: Hold the filing until the delay affidavit is actually supported, then file the appeal and the s. 5 application together
terminalOutcome.rationale: An unsupported s. 5 application is the single most common way these appeals die. 'Counsel did not file' is an assertion; a dated call log is a case. The appeal itself is decent, which makes the delay application the whole file.
terminalOutcome.nextAction: Take a dated delay statement from the client today, apply for certified copies, and file appeal and application together once the affidavit can be sworn truthfully.

teachingNotes: An expert's first question on a delay file is never 'is the delay condonable' — it is 'what does the client's own record show'. The client's conduct decides it, not the previous advocate's.
Eleven months with zero filing is not 'counsel was preparing'. The application must account for the months, not the reason.
Do not make the previous advocate a party. He is a witness, not a respondent, and a letter asking for the record creates the paper trail without a sideshow.
The engine blocks the client affidavit outright. That is the correct refusal — an affidavit sworn from memory about dates is worse than no affidavit.
commonMistakes: Filing the appeal with a one-line 'counsel failed to file' explanation.
Waiting for the previous advocate to respond before doing anything.
Framing grounds on the weight of the 1987 settlement when the trial court excluded it on a legal ground.
Filing the appeal without the certified decree, so it is listed defective and the delay grows.
seniorVariants: Build the s. 5 affidavit around the client's own follow-up record, annexed, with the previous advocate's non-response as corroboration rather than as the case.
Frame the first ground on the exclusion of the settlement as a legal error going to admissibility, not as a weighing error.
Send the letter to the previous advocate for the trial record and a no-objection, and file without waiting for a reply.
Check execution status first — if the decree is under execution, an application to stay execution is as urgent as the appeal itself.

accuracy.adverseFact: The 1987 family settlement is a photocopy. If it was never proved or was held to require registration, the trial court's exclusion may be correct and the principal ground collapses.
